title: Harborlane retail pilot — integration scratchpad
content:
Kickoff / context
- Company: Harborlane (regional retail chain, ~180 stores).
- Use case: in-store assistant for returns + inventory lookup + conversational POS helper. Low-latency requirement (p95 < 120ms for short queries), occasional long-running summarization jobs batched off-peak.
- Pilot footprint: 12 pilot stores, mixed connectivity (store kiosks behind NAT, some on flaky LTE backup).

Attendees (2025-11-03):
- Tom Reynolds (CTO)
- Priya Shah (Head of ML Ops)
- Anika Patel (Store Ops lead)
- Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CS lead)
- Ethan Brooks (Redwood Solutions eng)

High-level objectives for pilot:
- Demonstrate <120ms p95 on intent classification and short generation (<=64 tokens) for kiosk flows.
- Validate private deployment model (VPC + egress control) with no customer PII leaving their network.
- Exercise fallback/rollout policy: hosted -> dedicated -> private depending on latency/cost.
- Capture integration gotchas and produce runbook for roll to 100+ stores.

Notes / call capture (raw):
- Priya: "can't have customer data go to public endpoints; logs must be retained in-house for 1 year." PCI mention — follow-up with security checklist.
- Tom: keen on using Dedicated for predictable throughput but wants ability to burst to Hosted (cost tradeoffs). Wants deterministic routing policy.
- Anika: concerns about kiosk OS (custom Android image), app restart kills local cache; needs quick warmup strategies.
- Observed network pattern: stores have 80–150ms baseline RTT to us (us-east), but some have 300–600ms spikes on LTE fallback. That kills p95 target if we rely on cloud-hosted only.

Technical gotchas / flags:
- Kiosk environment: ARM-based CPUs for local fallback container; we need to confirm if private on-prem package supports ARM runtime. ACTION: check runtime/arm compatibility.
- KV cache: customer prefers local prefix caching to avoid repeated prompts on short flows. Need to validate KV eviction semantics when kiosk restarts.
- Tokenization mismatch: their preprocessor strips punctuation aggressively; risk of hallucinations for multi-line receipts. Recommend adding micro-eval set.
- TLS + mTLS: Harborlane requires mutual TLS for any control-plane interactions. Red team needs to confirm Private control plane supports mTLS and KMS integration for key rotation.
- Offline mode: kiosks must survive intermittent connectivity by queuing requests; design decision: allow degraded local LLM (small quantized model) vs queueing to on-prem cluster.
- Latency tail risk from autoscaling cold-starts on Dedicated pools; recommend warm-pool for pilot.

Pilot success metrics (agreed):
- Functional: >=95% correctness on 50-sample intent test suite (priors provided by Priya).
- Perf: p95 latency <120ms for <=64 token responses during business hours (measured at kiosk).
- Reliability: failover to private local inference within 2s when cloud unreachable.
- Ops: runbook with clear steps for rollback, canary increment, and incident triage.

Short-term next steps (owner/due):
- S1: Confirm ARM runtime support + on-prem packaging constraints (Ethan) — due 2025-11-10.
- S2: Share micro-eval dataset template; get 50 labeled intents from Priya (Sofia -> Priya) — due 2025-11-12.
- S3: Security checklist: mTLS, KMS integration, audit log retention (Security eng) — internal ticket RW-SEC-412 (Sofia) — due 2025-11-14.
- S4: Network characterization: sample RTTs from 12 pilot stores (Harborlane ops) — due 2025-11-07.
- S5: Prototype local fallback plan (quantized 7B on kiosk) feasibility doc + perf estimates (Ethan/Solutions) — due 2025-11-18.

Longer-term considerations / architecture options (brainstorm):
- Option A: Private on-prem cluster per region with routing policy "local first, then dedicated, then hosted". Pros: lowest latency, full data control. Cons: higher ops for Harborlane.
- Option B: Dedicated pool in customer VPC with lightweight local agent for prefix caching + short-run local quantized model for offline mode. Pros: balanced ops/cost.
- Option C: Fully hosted with edge CDN + aggressive prefix caching — likely fails compliance requirement re: PII.

Integration checklist (pre-demo):
- API key & secrets exchange (mTLS certs)
- Test dataset loaded into eval harness
- Canary plan: start 2 stores -> 12 stores -> +k 
- Alerting hooks: connect store-level alerts to Harborlane PagerDuty
- Cost telemetry demo: show token-level breakdown for kiosk flows

Open questions (to resolve on next call):
1) Do they prefer logs to be delivered to their S3 vs kept behind Redwoods' private control plane? (affects retention implementation)
2) Which kiosk devices/names make up the 12-store pilot (need device images/specs)?
3) Acceptable fallback behavior for payments flow if inference unavailable — must be synchronous / human fallback?
4) Legal: exact wording for data processing addendum for pilot vs production.

Meeting artifacts / refs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/cpg/harborlane-onramp (design notes, will append test cases)
- Jira: JIRA-RW-2378 (pilot epic)
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/4789 (work-in-progress: arm-startup-warm-pool)

Quick notes to self:
- Emphasize warm pools for Dedicated in the pilot deck.
- Build a small "handoff checklist" for store ops (how to restart kiosk without clearing KV).
- Put priors from Priya into eval harness asap — easiest way to show wins.

Next sync: 2025-11-10, 11am PT (follow-up on ARM + network samples).

-- end scratchpad (keep informal)
